solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stupid person lacking emotion, twisted inside

indicators.note: the interior of the word is twisted round, its two middle letters swapping places

parts.note: someone lacking emotion is cold, unfeeling

explanation.surface: A dim, unfeeling person who is also warped within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted inside' swaps the inner pair of COLD, so the O moves after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a dull, oafish dolt, literally a lump of earth.

clue.text: Mineral? You'd need firmness of character to have litre

parts.note: having backbone or a spine means having resolve

explanation.surface: A stern remark that strength of will is needed to handle a litre of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinel is a hard crystalline mineral, magnesium aluminium oxide, sometimes used as a gem.

clue.text: Dynamic type admitting excellent study is a success in a particular field

definitions.text: a success in a particular field

indicators.note: letting something in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a mover is an energetic, go-getting person
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A go-getter who lets in some good study time achieves success in their chosen area.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'particular field' is a cricket field: a maiden over is six balls bowled with no runs scored, a triumph for the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, bowling an over that concedes no runs is a notable achievement for the bowler on the pitch.

clue.text: Any poem can be stirring except for a 'Maud', say?

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters up, signalling a rearrangement
tells us one piece is left out of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A claim that any poem can rouse, apart from Tennyson's 'Maud'.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix ANYPOEM after taking out A. Tennyson's poem 'Maud' is named after its heroine, who therefore is an example of the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Maud is the character whose name gives the poem its title, so she is a namesake-giver of that work.

clue.text: Settle two opponents at table? Fine!

parts.note: at the bridge table East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N
the second of the two bridge seats, North
a sconce is an Oxford college penalty imposed for a breach of table manners

explanation.surface: Two rival card players at the table settle a matter and cry 'Fine!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine!' looks like agreement but is a noun: a sconce was a forfeit at Oxford college dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce oneself is to settle comfortably and securely in a place.

clue.text: Domestic delight in short supply

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to charm is to delight

explanation.surface: Domestic pleasures are rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' is a noun here: a household cleaner. A char or charwoman is British for a daily cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a cleaning woman, a household servant or domestic worker.

clue.text: Water is swirling around one plant

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the other piece
swirling water churns, so the letters are churned

parts.note: taken as written for mixing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Water eddies round a single plant in a garden pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' mixes WATERIS into WSTERIA; 'around' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging clusters of lilac flowers.

clue.text: Difficult Aussie man not primarily one to be dictated to

indicators.note: a difficult arrangement suggests the letters must be worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for mixing

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so take the opening letter of not

explanation.surface: An awkward Australian who is not essentially someone to take orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not primarily' pretends to negate; it supplies N, mixed in with AUSSIEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary who writes down what is spoken, taking dictation.

clue.text: Old coins forged from plate

indicators.note: metal that is forged is hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Ancient money counterfeited from a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepta were small coins of ancient Greece, the plural of lepton.

clue.text: Form of belief is held by those people following pagan god

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the god in the answer

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and wild places

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A creed held by followers of a pagan deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the doctrine that God is identical with the universe, a religious creed.

clue.text: A lot of sand and noise in NZ

definitions.note: a place in New Zealand: the definition names the city by its location

parts.note: a dune is a heap of sand
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A beach scene of sand and racket in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare location: the answer is a place found in NZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city on the South Island of New Zealand, founded by Scottish settlers.

clue.text: Tinned bread as source of vitamin A

indicators.note: joins the pieces; the putting-inside is really implied by 'Tinned', bread that has been tinned sits within its container

parts.note: a tin is a can, so tinned points to the container that holds the bread
roti is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Canned bread presented as a supply of vitamin A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinned' does double work, naming the container and implying the bread is sealed within it; roti is an Indian flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotin (carotene) is the orange pigment in carrots that the body converts to vitamin A.

clue.text: Stop people settling in another country endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a colony is a group of settlers abroad

explanation.surface: A call to halt migrants moving abroad without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is a noun: a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-dot punctuation mark is one of the stops used in writing.

clue.text: Construed as 'ancient', a people yielding to the Jews

indicators.note: construed means interpreted or arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient people seen as giving way to the Israelites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of the definition but is the last bit of fodder: AS ANCIENT A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaanites were the people of Canaan, conquered by the Israelites in the biblical account.

clue.text: Workers coming to a good lake for beasts

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Labourers arrive at a fine lake to see wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition.

clue.text: What may frustrate MPs, being group inside beset by craftiness

indicators.note: surrounded by, so the other pieces sit within

parts.note: guile means cunning
a lot is a group or batch
in means inside

explanation.surface: Parliament's frustration as a cabal works within, surrounded by cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the guillotine is a motion fixing a time limit on debate, cutting MPs short.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary time-limit motion curtails debate, so members cannot speak at length on a bill.

clue.text: Cave-maintainers, itinerant pre-modern people

indicators.note: wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Nomadic cave-dwellers from the ancient past.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous peoples of the Americas lived there long before modern European settlement.

clue.text: Souvenir? Could be kind with false front

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a face can be a facade, a show put on

explanation.surface: Is a keepsake a kindness with an insincere front?
explanation.walkthrough: Souvenir is a font name, not a keepsake; the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvenir is the name of a font design, so it is an instance of a printed lettering style.

clue.text: Scan tale furiously for literary passages

indicators.note: frantic activity, suggesting the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Reading a story at speed to find good extracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Analects are selected extracts from writings, as in the Analects of Confucius.

clue.text: A sign 'inders what it's supposed to represent

parts.note: hinders with its h dropped is 'ampers, cockney for hampers
the & symbol stands for the word and

explanation.surface: A sign that obstructs what it is meant to stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe signals a dropped H, as in cockney speech: 'inders is 'ampers.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol is a typographical sign used in place of a conjunction.

clue.text: Abandon course being a bit gutted

indicators.note: a little of the inside is removed, one middle letter

parts.note: dessert is the sweet course of a meal

explanation.surface: Giving up a race track that is somewhat hollowed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to leave behind or forsake.

clue.text: Destructive creature finds a place, losing little time

indicators.note: giving up a letter, which is removed

parts.note: a locust strips crops bare
T is a short form of time

explanation.surface: A crop-destroying insect finds somewhere, dropping a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for a position or site.

clue.text: Sway in church? Traditionalists may not like it

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to hang is to dangle and sway

explanation.surface: Swaying in the pews is something conservative churchgoers frown on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of worship, but 'Sway' is the inserted piece and 'church' the abbreviation that holds it; the definition is the whole second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives resist alteration of any kind, preferring things to stay as they are.

clue.text: Balloon at someone's home, first hint of excitement

parts.note: in flat means at home in an apartment

indicators.note: just the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A balloon at a friend's place, the first sign of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' is a verb: to swell up.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell or expand, as when air is blown in.

clue.text: Chemical coming from a chimney on the Clyde?

parts.note: lum is the Scots word for a chimney; the Clyde is Glasgow's river

explanation.surface: A substance belching from a smokestack in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a double sulphate salt used in dyeing and tanning.

clue.text: Problem fire trapping French and British

indicators.note: enclosing, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A blaze that traps people from France and Britain is a real problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse or difficulty that holds back progress.

clue.text: Outfit beginning to explore a device for testing public opinion

definitions.text: a device for testing public opinion

parts.note: kit means a set of clothes or equipment

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Equipment for a first look at a gadget for sampling public views.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly a kite is to float an idea to test reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying a kite means floating a proposal to gauge how people react to it.

clue.text: Meeting death almost, having to fight

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: end can mean death
to counter is to oppose or fight back

explanation.surface: A brush with death that becomes a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, especially an unexpected or hostile one.

clue.text: The dark rider heading off

indicators.note: the head, its first letter, comes off

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior

explanation.surface: The sinister horseman rides away.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is what falls after sunset, the hours between dusk and dawn.
